A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TAG research, with matching authors, core algorithm, theorem, and retained illustrations. The main text and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial expansion and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-generation evaluations in Tables 1–5, synthetic branching-distribution experiments in Figure 3, ablations, and additional generated examples in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 reports original image-generation, compositional-faithfulness, video, and sensitivity results, plus SSG, EDM2, and qualitative image-to-3D experiments in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The core radial/tangential projection remains unchanged. Section 6.1 adds timestep-windowed application and norm-adaptive conditional amplification, which v1 only contemplated as future work. The conditional implementation also separates the TAG coefficient from the CFG coefficient, aligning it with v1's pseudocode and resolving inconsistent documentation. These are limited extensions and corrections to the retained sampler.

E1.justification: v2 adds compositional generation on T2I-CompBench Spatial and Complex, text-to-video generation on VBench prompts, and a qualitative image-to-3D test with SV3D. ImageNet and COCO remain represented, although COCO replaces ImageNet as the reference dataset for the main unconditional comparisons. The new compositional requirements and output modalities substantially broaden coverage.

E2.justification: v2 newly evaluates APG and TCFG in Table 6, UniPC in Table 9, and Self-Swap Guidance in Table 13. APG and TCFG were previously discussed but not experimentally compared. The SAG comparison rows from v1 Table 1 disappear, while PAG, SEG, CFG, and DPM++ remain in revised comparisons.

E3.justification: Reported settings change substantially: unconditional PAG/SEG compatibility uses PNDM instead of DDIM, conditional compatibility moves from SD1.5 to SDXL, and unconditional SD2.1/SDXL sample counts increase from 10K to 30K. FID computation changes from pytorch-fid to torch-fidelity. v2 adds aesthetic, preference, CMMD, compositional, perceptual-quality, and video metrics, alongside new windowing and adaptive-scaling protocols. These changes prevent direct comparison of many cross-version scores.

E4.justification: v2 adds analyses of when TAG should operate along the trajectory and whether adaptive normalization reduces amplification sensitivity (Tables 11–12). Computational analysis expands from latency to FLOPs, memory, and overhead, while Appendix C adds prompt-specific object and action error comparisons. The qualitative amplification sweep remains, but v1's numerical unconditional amplification curve is removed.

E5.justification: v2 newly specifies per-image seeds 0–29,999 for unconditional generation and seed 0 for conditional generation; this does not establish additional independent repetitions. v1's CLIPScore ± reporting disappears, while v2 Table 9 introduces IS ± values without explaining their statistical meaning. The earlier statement that latency averages 100 consecutive runs is also absent.

E6.justification: Benchmark results are extensively replaced and expanded under revised conditions. New Table 6 reports TAGcfg/APG/TCFG FID values of 19.29/19.52/20.72, with APG leading CLIPScore. Table 7 reports improved Qwen-Image perceptual scores but worse FID, 57.53 to 59.84. The original full-window SD1.5/DDIM FID of 67.805 survives in Table 11, alongside a new restricted-window result of 63.870. These are added findings, not evidence of uniform same-setting improvement over v1.

T1.justification: Theorem 4.1 and its Appendix A proof are substantially retained. v2 adds an explicit step-budget constraint to the local optimization in Equation 11 and corrects the main theorem's equality condition to match v1's appendix. The exact squared-norm identity explaining radial perturbation in v1 Equation 21 is removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: tangential updates carry semantic structure, their amplification promotes local likelihood gain, and TAG improves generation without retraining or additional denoiser evaluations. Broader experiments support these claims without materially redefining the headline contribution.

C2.justification: v1 emphasizes excessive amplification disturbing radial calibration. v2 develops a thin-shell interpretation, explains adaptive scaling and heuristic windowing, and explicitly limits the theory to local first-order gain rather than complete trajectory behavior. It also acknowledges approximate manifold geometry, interprets compositional and video findings, and discusses the perceptual-quality/FID tradeoff on Qwen-Image and the preliminary nature of 3D evidence.

D1.justification: Appendix F adds substantial reproducibility information beyond v1's brief software statement and code snippets: package/CUDA versions, GPU configuration, pipeline integration, guidance layers, SEG blur and SSG swap parameters, metric implementations, resizing, reference sets, and execution details. These disclosures do not by themselves establish changed experiments. Some conditional hyperparameters remain unspecified.

R1.justification: Appendix E and Table 15 substantially expand research positioning, comparing the projected quantities, subspaces, objectives, and costs of TAG, APG, TCFG, Characteristic Guidance, Perp-Neg, MPGD, and SDDM. Newly cited literature also supports the expanded benchmarks, models, metrics, and Gaussian-shell motivation. This goes well beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The experimental narrative is extensively rewritten and divided into new subsections; discussion is expanded, and conclusions and limitations are combined. Implementation material moves from Appendix B to D, with broader experiments, detailed positioning, and experimental documentation organized into additional appendices. The motivation is expanded, the title shortened, and C-TAG renamed TAGcfg.

P2.justification: v2 changes the main paper from single-column to two-column layout and substantially restructures tables and figure placement. It adds a geometric schematic, video and 3D illustrations, extensive comparison galleries, and methodological comparison/settings tables. v1 Figure 9 is retained as v2 Figure 10; the qualitative amplification panels remain with revised labels, while their accompanying numerical plot is removed.

improvement.justification: v1 supports hallucination reduction mainly through general image-quality metrics and selected examples. v2 substantially strengthens that evidence with targeted compositional tests and direct APG/TCFG comparisons (Tables 5–6), while fuller implementation documentation and explicit theoretical limitations make the work easier to assess. These gains outweigh lost CLIPScore dispersion and reduced-NFE comparison detail, although incomplete conditional settings and unexplained uncertainty estimates remain weaknesses.
